Comment: Arizona objected to the general implication under Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action that there is "general public agreement and identification with the proposed legislation."
Response: Wording of this section of the EIS was not intended to reflect general public sentiment for or against the proposed legislation. We agree that the EIS should not indicate support for or against the proposed legislation, and this has been one of the objectives of revision of the draft. The Office of Endangered Species received over 20,000 pieces of mail in FY 1972 of which practically all expressed some degree of support for endangered species preservation.
Review of the comments being discussed herein from States and Federal agencies suggests much more favorable than unfavorable sentiment.
<u>Comment:</u> The letter contends that contrary to the draft environmental statement, there is an irreversible or irretreivable commitment of resources in that production lost from land set aside for endangered species here is irretreivable in terms of time.
Response: We agree with the suggestion, and have modified the appropriate section to reflect the loss of time as a commitment.
